title: gpu-rop-and-sla-allocation-notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a pragmatic reorder-point (ROP) and SLA allocation approach for the GPU fleet. The goal is to provide a repeatable method that maps customer-facing SLAs and regional traffic patterns to concrete SKU-level reorder triggers, safety stock cushions, and prioritized order lanes. This is intended to replace ad-hoc email requests with a defendable, data-driven plan.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Use a per-SKU, per-region ROP computed from observed burn and lead-time variance.
- Apply SLA tranching: Tier-A (99% availability target) gets a higher z-factor and emergency reorder lane; Tier-B and C get progressively lower buffers.
- Maintain a small cross-region pool of fungible SKUs (H100 and A100 family) for 30-day emergency runway.
- For ordering, split procurements into (1) firm committed capacity, (2) optional burst tranche, (3) spot/lease overlay.

Key definitions and formulas: (simple, reproducible)
- Average demand (D_avg) = mean GPUs consumed per day (per SKU-region).
- Lead time (L) = supplier lead time in days (order to rack-ready). Use median historical lead time and track 75th/90th percentiles.
- Demand variability during lead time sigma_LD = sqrt(L) * sigma_daily (approx for iid daily demand).
- Reorder point (ROP) = D_avg * L + z * sigma_LD
  - where z = safety factor (z-score) based on SLA target.
  - Example z-values used in this doc: Tier-A (99%) z=2.33, Tier-B (95%) z=1.645, Tier-C (90%) z=1.282.

Practical adjustments we apply: (not purely statistical)
- Minimum absolute safety stock floor: no SKU-region ROP < 6 units (enough for short-term swaps).
- Granularity: round ROP up to order multiples (e.g., vendor packs of 4).
- Lead time uplift: add a fixed +10% to lead time when suppliers are in backlog mode (supplier watchlist flag).
- Fungibility credit: when a region has a fungible pool and cross-region transfer SLA allows, reduce per-region ROP by up to 20% and keep the fungible pool at dedicated buffer levels.

Current snapshot (sample SKUs and computed runways) — snapshot date: 2026-02-15:
SKU  | on_hand | committed | weekly_burn | days_runway (on_hand/weekly_burn*7)
H100-80GB | 72 | 40 | 56 | 9
A100-80GB | 104 | 60 | 80 | 9
L40       | 210 | 30 | 70 | 21
T4        | 430 | 120 | 210 | 14

Observations from snapshot:
- H100 and A100 runway under 10 days in peak clusters — triggers ROP injections for Tier-A capacity lanes.
- L40 and T4 are bulk capacity; runway is more comfortable but committed orders are rising.

Lead-time matrix (supplier-level):
- Supplier X (primary): median 28 days, 75th pct 38d, 90th pct 55d.
- Supplier Y (secondary): median 21d, 75th pct 30d, 90th pct 44d.
- Lease/spot overlay: lead time ~3-7d (availability varies).

Example ROP computation (H100, us-west):
- D_avg = 8 GPUs/day (us-west H100 burn)
- sigma_daily = 3.1 GPUs/day
- L (use median +10% uplift) = 28 * 1.10 = 30.8 -> round to 31 days
- sigma_LD = sqrt(31) * 3.1 ≈ 17.3
- Tier-A z = 2.33 -> ROP = 8 * 31 + 2.33 * 17.3 ≈ 248 + 40.3 ≈ 289 GPUs -> order multiple => 292 (packs of 4)
- Action: if available_on_hand + incoming_committed < ROP then raise procurement ticket for firm order + optional burst tranche.

SLA tranche mapping (recommended):
- Tier-A (prod-critical): availability target 99% -> z=2.33, emergency reorder lane (expedite shipments), dedicated committed capacity in region (reserve pool).
- Tier-B (high priority): 95% -> z=1.645, optional burst lane available if capacity permits.
- Tier-C (non-critical / dev): 90% -> z=1.282, rely more on spot overlay, cross-region transfers.

Order lane design (how we actually place orders):
- Firm committed orders: baseline long-lead purchases to keep committed capacity above ROP for Tier-A and B. Week-by-week cadence reviewed every 2 weeks.
- Optional burst tranche: negotiable add-on to firm orders (vendor options) that can be exercised if last-week runway < threshold (14 days for Tier-A).
- Lease/spot overlay: short-term cover for sudden bursts; used sparingly due to cost.
- Emergency expedite lane: flyaway or priority shipping for outages impacting SLAs. Pre-approve $X cost threshold per region to avoid exec slowdown.

Scenario planning (three canonical stress tests):
1) Baseline: current burn, normal lead times. Expected runway aligns with snapshot.
2) Double-burn surge: demand x2 for 30 days (product feature launch). Impact: H100 runway drops to ~4 days; trigger immediate exercise of optional burst and spot overlay; expedite at supplier for critical clusters.
3) Supplier delay shock: supplier X lead times +25% for 60 days. Impact: recompute ROP with uplift, move to priority lane for Tier-A SKUs, accelerate secondary supplier orders with split shipments.

Metric triggers to automate procurement signals: (to implement in procurement dashboard)
- Runway <= 14 days for Tier-A -> create auto procurement ticket with proposed quantities to restore to ROP + 30%.
- Week-over-week committed increase > 30% -> flag for capacity re-eval and possible SKU mix shift.
- Lead-time 75th pct > 45d for any primary supplier -> move to contingency purchasing (split across suppliers).

Regional fungibility rules (practical):
- Define fungible pools for H100/A100 by region pairings (us-west <-> us-central, eu-west <-> eu-north). Transfers allowed if cold-start transfer time < 72 hours and cross-region network setup is validated.
- Cross-region transfer cost cap: per-transfer cost must not exceed 8% of replacement unit cost for moves to be auto-approved.

Procurement playbook snippets (checklist style):
- Pre-order: vendor quotes attached, lead time percentile, packing multiple, customs windows, expected arrival date window.
- Post-order: assign delivery SLA owner, schedule staging window (48h slack), confirm Kitting and labelling.
- On-delay: if shipment misses 75th pct estimate, trigger supplier call and open expedite option; notify product owners.

Open questions / discussion items:
- How to model correlated demand spikes across regions (we currently assume independence for sigma_LD). Need a simple correlation factor to inflate sigma when cross-region campaigns occur.
- Should we set different absolute minimum safety stock floors by SKU weight/MTTR? e.g., A100 min=4, H100 min=6, L40 min=12.
- Funding approval: threshold for auto-expedites without exec sign-off (current proposal: $200k/region).

Immediate next steps (owners):
- (Liam) Build per-SKU, per-region ROP calculator in the procurement dashboard (data source: inventory, committed orders, weekly burn). Due: 2026-03-05.
- (Aisha) Validate supplier lead-time percentiles and add supplier watchlist flags. Due: 2026-02-28 (in progress).
- (Marco) Draft cross-region fungible pool runbook and transfer cost estimators. Due: 2026-03-12.

Appendix — quick worked example for a 30-day surge plan:
- If product signals +100% baseline burn for 30 days on us-west H100: pre-bid optional burst tranche = 0.6 * surge demand (covers partial surge cheaply), spot overlay reserved = 0.4 * surge demand, expedite reserved if runway < 7d after those actions.

Notes and references:
- Link to procurement ticket template: confluence://procurement/gpu-order-template
- Related Jira: INFRA-412 (visibility to committed orders), INFRA-433 (procurement dashboard feature request).

End of note.
